cards.name: Arrowhead
cards.summary: Turns the one selected vector object or artistic-text object into a custom arrowhead and adds it to the start / end arrowhead pickers of the Outline pen and property bar. Opens the Create Arrowhead dialog first; the drawing itself is left unchanged.
use_for: brand-specific arrow tips for diagrams and infographics
custom line endings for maps, flowcharts and callout leaders
a logo mark reused as a line terminator
avoid: more than one object or a bitmap selected: the command is disabled; combine the parts into one curve first
a one-off arrow drawn as artwork: just draw the shape, a registered arrowhead is only worth it when reused
cards.how: Select exactly one curve, shape or artistic text (the harvest enables it only for a single vector or artistic text object), run the command, set the arrowhead size in the dialog (length / width, proportional or not) and confirm. The new head then appears at the end of the arrowhead lists; apply it to a line from the property bar or the Outline Pen dialog.

Object model (unverified): ActiveShape.CreateArrowHead, or ActiveDocument.CreateArrowHead2(curve, name); then assign it with Shape.Outline.EndArrow / StartArrow.

cards.name: Pattern Fill
cards.summary: Captures part of the drawing as a new pattern tile (vector or bitmap) and saves it as a reusable pattern fill. Opens a dialog to choose the pattern type before you mark the area to capture.
use_for: seamless brand patterns for packaging, gift wrap and backgrounds
turning a motif into a fill for textile or wallpaper mock-ups
repeat backgrounds for social posts and stationery
avoid: tiles that must line up seamlessly without testing: check the repeat at the edges after applying the fill
a bitmap pattern when the output is large-format print: capture as a vector pattern so it stays sharp
cards.how: With a document open, run the command, choose Vector or Bitmap pattern (and resolution for a bitmap one) in the dialog, then marquee the area or click the objects that make up one tile and confirm; the pattern is saved and becomes available in the fill picker for vector / bitmap pattern fills.

cards.name: Fit Objects to Path
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Fit Objects to Path docker, which arranges the selected objects (or copies of them) along a path: spacing, rotation to follow the path and extra copies are set in the docker. The same command sits at Window > Dockers > Fit Objects to Path. Menu visibility is bound to WPasmDataSource.CanLoadBinariesOutsideInstallFolder (it was visible in this install).
use_for: icons or dots running around a circular badge or seal
decorative borders built from one ornament
type-free repeats along a curve: footprints, stitches, chain links
avoid: text along a curve: use Text > Fit Text to Path, which keeps the text editable
an even repeat of identical copies along a straight line: Step and Repeat is simpler
cards.how: Open the docker, select the objects to distribute together with the guide path, then set the options the docker exposes (harvested from its data source: arrange by, even gaps, rotate to follow the path and centre of rotation, extra copies, spin and angle jitter, keep originals, group after) and apply. Which selected object is used as the path is decided by the docker; check its prompt.

cards.name: Group

use_for: keeping a logo lockup together while laying out a poster
moving a whole illustration or icon as one piece
applying one transformation or PowerClip to several objects
avoid: merging shapes into one outline: use Combine (one curve) or Shaping > Weld instead
a selection that mixes objects from inside different groups: the harvest's enable rule (AreSelectedNodesFromDiffGroups) disables Group then

taking apart a placed or imported file one level at a time
avoid: deeply nested imports (PDF / SVG / EPS): use Ungroup All to flatten every level at once

cards.name: Barcode
cards.summary: Starts the Barcode Wizard to build a linear barcode (retail and industrial symbologies) from the number you enter and places it on the page as a barcode object. Hidden when the app runs sandboxed (IsSandboxedApp); enabled only when the barcode component is present (IsBarCodeAppExist), the active layer is editable and you are not in full-screen preview, the page sorter or a PowerClip edit.
use_for: EAN / UPC barcodes on packaging and labels
inventory or asset labels
tickets and coupons that need a scannable code
avoid: QR codes: use Object > Insert > QR Code

cards.how: Run the command, pick the barcode standard in the wizard, type the digits (the wizard checks length and check digit for the chosen standard), set size / resolution and the human-readable text options, then finish to place it.

cards.name: Join Curves
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Join Curves docker, which joins the end nodes of selected open curves that lie within a gap tolerance into one curve, using the join method you choose. Also at Window > Dockers > Join Curves.
use_for: closing traced outlines so they can take a fill
repairing imported CAD or PDF line work broken into segments
joining hand-drawn strokes into one path for cutting plotters
avoid: joining shapes into one object without touching nodes: use Combine
a tolerance that is too large: distant ends get bridged and the shape distorts
cards.how: Open the docker, select the curves to join, set the gap tolerance (how far apart end nodes may be) and the join method, then apply. Handy after tracing or importing CAD / PDF line work that arrives as many broken segments.

cards.name: Object Hinting
cards.summary: Check toggle that aligns the selected objects to the pixel grid (its binding is AlignToPixel) so their edges land on whole pixels and render crisp, not anti-aliased and blurry, in pixel exports.

avoid: print artwork: pixel alignment only helps pixel (screen / PNG) output; leave it off for print
rotated or curved shapes: they cannot sit fully on the grid, so the gain is small

cards.name: Objects
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Objects docker: the tree of pages, layers and objects where you select, rename, reorder, hide, lock and move objects between layers. Also at Window > Dockers > Objects.
use_for: managing layers in a multi-page brochure or packaging dieline
selecting objects buried under others
renaming and organizing objects before handing a file over
avoid: simple restacking of one object: the Order commands (Ctrl+PageUp / PageDown) are faster
cards.how: Toggle it on, then work in the tree: click to select (including locked or hidden objects), drag to restack or move between layers, and use the eye / lock icons per object or layer.
